items.text: SCRIPT, a trial led by the universities of Bern and Lucerne with the participating cities, sells cannabis with counselling through pharmacies in Bern and Biel (and in Lucerne). Planned from May 2024 to April 2026, with up to 1,091 participants across the three cities; the federal list still showed it on 3 November 2026.

Under the federal pilot-trial rules, only adults who live in this canton and can show they already use cannabis may enrol. Participants may use the products only themselves: no passing them on and no use in publicly accessible places. Visitors from outside the canton can't enrol or buy, and the national cannabis ban applies to everyone outside the trials. Each trial is limited to five years, with one extension of up to two years possible; the legal basis for the trials ends on 14 May 2031.

Federal-approved cannabis pilot trial here: SCRIPT (Bern and Biel): non-profit sale in pharmacies with counselling. Pilot trials are scientific studies approved by the federal health office; organisers report to it yearly.

laws.rule: Anyone staying overnight in the canton of Bern pays a cantonal accommodation levy (Beherbergungsabgabe), collected by the host. The law sets it between CHF 0.50 and CHF 1.50 a night (about A$0.86 to A$2.59) (art. 22(1)); the canton's tourism page gives CHF 1 a night for guests over 16 (about A$1.73). It is not charged for children under 16, short-stay residents, military or civil protection billeting, or in hospitals and care homes (art. 21). Stays are covered up to three months (art. 20(2)). Municipalities can add their own Kurtaxe and tourism promotion levy on top. AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = CHF 0.5789.

laws.rule: Dogs in Bern must be on a lead on school grounds, public playgrounds and sports fields, on public transport, at stations and stops, and when entering pastures with livestock; also where there is no other effective control, and where an authority orders it. Municipalities can name more lead places (art. 7(1)-(2)). Hunting and nature-protection lead rules also apply (art. 7(4)). Breaches are punished with a fine (art. 15).
laws.heading: Hundegesetz (BSG 916.31), arts 7 and 15

laws.rule: Bern has a public holiday rest law. Sundays and public holidays are rest days: any activity that disturbs church services or substantially disturbs the quiet is banned, and door-to-door and van selling are banned (art. 3). Public holidays are Sundays, Good Friday, Easter, Ascension, Whit Sunday, the Federal Day of Thanksgiving, Repentance and Prayer, Christmas, New Year's Day, 2 January, Easter Monday, Whit Monday, 1 August and 26 December (art. 2). On the high holidays (Good Friday, Easter, Ascension, Pentecost, Bettag, Christmas) large non-religious events, large outdoor concerts without a reflective character, shows and gambling for money are also banned (art. 4). Pubs and restaurants follow the hospitality law instead (art. 5). Municipalities enforce it and can allow exceptions (arts 7 and 8); breaches are fined (art. 11).
